reflection.text:
Unblinded truth: Epithelial, Agent final: Actin disruptors (0.42) - VERDICT FALSE. Previous Eg5 call (0.52) also false.

What the evidence got right: There was a real, monotonic phenotype. e2 (1uM, 1036 cells) -> e3 (10uM, 661 cells) -> e7 (30uM 114 cells) shows dose-dependent cell loss (e13 rho -1.00), dose-dependent increase in frac_large_nucleus (e8 rho +1.00, z +8.7 to +23.0 to +59.3), frac_mitotic_like (e9 rho +1.00), act_mean (e12 rho +1.00) and tub_mean (e10 rho +1.00) with very large actin/tubulin texture contrasts (act_glcm_contrast +9.8 to +21.7 to +77.8; tub_glcm_contrast +43.8 at 30uM) and reduced nuc_solidity (e14 rho -1.00). describe_phenotype e4 - density lower vs DMSO - was correct for cytotoxicity. The trends themselves were not artifact.

What misled and why:

1. compare_to_reference_atlas instability and collapsed-well weighting. e5 on the initial sampling (1uM+10uM) was Protein synthesis 4/10, Actin disruptors 3/10, Eg5 2/10 with top neighbor an actin-disruptor profile. e15 on the 30uM collapsed well (n=114, e7) flipped to Eg5 5/10, Actin 3/10. I updated hypotheses in e16 to Eg5 0.48 based on e7/e9/e10/e15 and submitted e17 Eg5 0.52 explicitly because 'Peak dose strong mitotic arrest and microtubule brightening best matches Eg5'. Review was correct: this rested on a single toxicity well where mean similarity was not reported and Eg5 plurality disappeared when re-running atlas on the highest non-collapsed well w_a94645f008 alone (e18 identical to e5: Protein synthesis 4/10, Actin 3/10, Eg5 2/10).

2. Over-interpretation of tub_mean/act_mean increases: e10 and e12 both rho +1.00 and e7 tub_glcm_contrast +43.8 were read as microtubule stabilization / Eg5 monoaster vs actin aggregation. In reality epithelial cytoskeletal remodeling also drives coordinated actin/tubulin intensity and texture changes via Rho-GAP / SEPT9-ARHGAP4-EMT type pathways - e.g. PMID 32378260 shows how epithelial state directly regulates actin organization - so these features are not specific to mitotic targets.

3. Ignored contradiction in nuc_area e11 rho -1.00. Eg5, Aurora, microtubule stabilizers and classic polyploidy should increase mean nuclear area, not decrease it. Median area falling while frac_large_nucleus rises implies heterogeneity + cell loss/fragmentation, not a pure monopolar arrest. I listed this as contradicting Aurora in e16 but did not apply it to Eg5.

What I missed:

I prematurely zeroed Epithelial. In both hypothesis updates e16 and e19 P(Epithelial)=0.0 with contradicting IDs e7/e4, and never restored a prior despite lookup_compound e21 returning no structure/mechanism for AZ-U (internal code, no PubChem/ChEMBL). With no chemical prior and an atlas that never returned Epithelial as nearest neighbor, I should have retained a non-zero prior and tested epithelial features directly - e.g. cell-cell junctions, cobblestone morphology, solidity changes at low dose (e6 cell_solidity +1.8, act_glcm_contrast -4.2) rather than only scoring large nuclei/mitotic-like fractions. The requested experiment e18 correctly showed Actin/Protein synthesis dominance at 10uM, so I switched to Actin disruptors e20, but still did not consider that actin texture + large irregular nuclei + viability drop can be downstream of epithelial regulation rather than direct actin depolymerization. Acquisition choice also contributed: sampling only 4 wells (0.1,1,10,30uM rep1) with no replicates and heavy weighting of the 30uM n=114 outlier left no ability to visually confirm monoasters/bundles vs failed cytokinesis - I proposed IF for pericentrin/p-H3 in conclusions but had no data to distinguish.

Lesson: keep all MOA priors >0 when compound is uncured, treat extreme z-scores in collapsed wells (n~100) as toxicity flag not MOA signal, and require atlas plurality at non-collapsed doses plus orthogonal validation before calling Eg5/Actin over Epithelial.

The requested experiment e18 correctly showed Actin/Protein synthesis dominance at 10uM, so I switched to Actin disruptors e20, but still did not consider that actin texture + large irregular nuclei + viability drop can be downstream of epithelial regulation rather than direct actin depolymerization. Lesson: keep all MOA priors >0 when compound is uncured, treat extreme z-scores in collapsed wells (n~100) as toxicity flag not MOA signal, and require atlas plurality at non-collapsed doses plus orthogonal validation before calling Eg5/Actin over Epithelial.

What was right:
- e13 rho -1.00 cell loss, e8 rho +1.00 frac_large_nucleus, e9 frac_mitotic_like, e10 tub_mean, e12 act_mean monotonic trends real with z increasing 8.7 to 23.0 to 59.3
- e4 density lower correct; e14 reduced solidity indicating irregular nuclei/polyploid population correct
- e5/e18 agreement that at non-collapsed doses Eg5 not plurality was correct signal ignored initially

What was wrong or missed:
- e15 Eg5 5/10 at 30uM n=114 over-weighted leading to e16/e17 Eg5 0.48/0.52
- Epithelial set to 0.0 in e16/e19 never revisited despite no chemical info e21
- e11 nuc_area rho -1.00 contradiction to polyploidy not applied to Eg5

Proposed next experiment: If real lab: low-toxicity doses 0.3-1uM high-res phalloidin/alpha-tubulin/E-cadherin/beta-catenin + DAPI to score cell-cell contacts/cobblestone vs monoasters/actin aggregates, plus junction integrity assay; not p-H3/centrosome alone.
